newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall; looking to U.S. jobless.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall; looking to U.S. jobless.

text.p: Argentine bonds fell slightly Thursday in calm trade ahead of the release of the important U.S. jobless report on Friday.
"There was a very small trading-range ahead of the U.S. figures," said a trader at a large foreign bank.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.15 to 115.90. Argentina's FRB due 2005 slipped 1/8 to 78-5/8.
Traders said worries over whether the U.S. jobless report will show signs of a strong economy overcame local influences.

President Carlos Menem held his much touted meeting of the Peronist Party Thursday where he delivered an impassioned speech in search of unity. The market is most interested in signs of whether Menem managed to convince his party to give its full support of the government's economic policies.
The trader said it was too early to tell what the reactions from Congressmen will be.
Still, "we liked what we saw from Menem," said another trader.
Even if the U.S. unemployment figures point to strong growth and higher U.S. rates, the traders said the market is well supported.
But, "it needs another push" to resume its recent upward trend, said the first trader.
In the money markets, one day call money rates fell to 8.05 percent from 8.15 percent.
